design.change: Introduce an explicit source constraint with ExactType as the default and RegisteredFamily as an opt-in for dependency declarations and dependency-only references. Register a family predicate under TypeID::ACTOR_DB from App DBRelations using dynamic_cast<const ActorDB*>. Document only stores/invokes the AutoRegisterDB predicate and never includes ActorDB.hpp.
contract: Preserve existing exact-type registration APIs/defaults and target matching. Ownership declarations and ownership references remain exact.
Unknown family, absent source, null source, or predicate mismatch fails closed. Validate referenced families at registration; register Actor family before widget declarations.
One reference declaration per child type and field remains enforced; matching mode participates in duplicate/conflict checks.

Family predicates are stateless type checks and cannot mutate the document or acquire document locks. Registry clear resets families as well as rules. Clear/re-register is supported only during initialization or a test reset after all document relation edges and chain updaters have been removed; it is not a live hot-reload mechanism. A repeated identical module registration without clear remains idempotent and retains rule IDs.

Within one relation/target/ruleName, exact-source match overrides a family match; different rule names remain additive. Multiple equally specific family matches for one logical rule fail with a diagnostic rather than firing duplicate callbacks. Resolve ambiguity before attaching any edge or updater.
Rule selection has stable ordering and retains selected registered rule IDs for updater identity. Family registration is initialization-only, not modified while dependencies are live.

design.change: Use the same source constraint matcher and instance-aware dependency resolver for reference-parent validation, current dependency-source discovery, DocumentManager attachment, and ChainUpdateSystem updater creation. Resolve objects before callbacks and avoid invoking predicates/callbacks under relation locks.
contract: Do not leave a type-only lookup path for family relations in one of these four entry points. Keep exact-only lookup compatible for existing callers/tests. The resolver takes actual TypeID metadata plus an optional real source instance; exact-only checks never dereference or dynamic-cast the source. The existing ChainUpdateRelationCheck int-backed alias pointers are identity placeholders only and cannot be cast to a real object; family tests must use safe real polymorphic objects.
A re-link from Actor A to Actor B removes A's edge and updater and creates exactly one B edge/updater; invalid-parent behavior remains explicit and leaves no stale active updater.
Preserve failed-attachment rollback, idempotent attachment, instance existence checks, deletion reasons and rebuilding from reference fields.

Keep existing exact-type static cycle checks; do not claim the TypeID graph proves absence of cycles through arbitrary family predicates. Runtime instance cycle detection, including self edges and reverse paths through a family, remains mandatory before attachment and applies to all attachment paths.

WidgetDB actually inherits AutoRegisterDB, not ActorDB. A widget used as an Actor-family source must be rejected by the predicate. Keep generic self-edge and family-cycle tests using appropriate test-only dependency declarations.

design.change: Register the ActorDB family and opt all four widget dependency/reference pairs into that same constraint. Keep selection-box WorldBounds and other widgets' Transform watches and existing ActorDB callbacks.
contract: Do not auto-create transform widgets for new actor types; this only fixes existing linked-widget relations.

Keep DerivedUpdateGuard on synchronous derived callbacks. Change deferred selection-box deletion to TransientUpdateGuard rather than a new TransactionGuard, adapting the already observed upstream cleanup correction.

Before deferred deletion, capture and re-check both deleted source ID and widget ID: the same widget must still be linked to that deleted source and the source must still be absent. A stale queued callback must not delete a restored/relinked selection box. Test with a QCoreApplication event loop.

Fix ModelInteractionHandler::createSelectionBox so a cached actor-to-widget entry prevents creation only when the actual SelectionBoxWidgetDB still exists and its LinkedActorID matches. Erase stale/mismatched entries and create the needed box without deleting another actor's valid box. Verify the actor exists before creating. SelectionBridge deletion currently removes selected IDs without clearing this map, so deletion/undo must not rely on that notification to clear it.

If a selection-visual restoration path reaches applySelection with unchanged IDs, validate/reconcile its visuals rather than assuming cached boxes exist. Do not change product selection semantics: undo need not automatically restore selection, but selecting a restored actor must recreate a valid box.
